subject: Launch volume phasing & monthly commit structure
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@launchlabs.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch volume phasing & commit Qs

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked great. We are planning a staged public launch in early October and expect a pretty steep usage curve during the first 6–8 weeks. A few numbers to start the conversation:

- Baseline expected tokens (pre-launch): ~1.5B tokens/mo
- Launch peak weeks (weeks 1–4 after launch): equivalent of ~15B tokens/mo peak (short spikes)
- Post-launch steady state (months 2–6): ~6–8B tokens/mo

Procurement expects a monthly commit agreement for the first 6 months and needs clarity on:
- Per-token pricing and how discounts scale with commit tiers
- Whether we can build a step-up commit schedule to match the launch ramp (so we don’t overpay early but can secure capacity)
- Overage treatment: true-up, credits, or per-token overage rate?
- Handling big short spikes during launch (burst protection / throttles)

Can you share a sample monthly commit ramp structure and any flexibility on discounts tied to commit velocity/seasonality? Also, procurement prefers monthly invoices.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product Operations | Launch Labs
procurement@launchlabs.com
Attachment: none
From: camila_reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch volume phasing & commit Qs

Elena — thanks for the detail, this is exactly the type of info we need. High-level response and a rough proposal attached (Launch_Labs_Monthly_Commit_v1.pdf):

Proposal highlights (draft):
- 6-month monthly commit with a 3-month intentional ramp (Sept, Oct, Nov):
  - Sept commit: 2.0B tokens (intro/off-peak prep)
  - Oct commit: 8.0B tokens (launch month primary)
  - Nov commit: 12.0B tokens (post-launch catch-up)
  - Dec–Feb commit: 6.0B tokens/mo steady state
- Discounting: per-token list price with volume tiers applied to each month’s commit. Example discounts: 5% @ >=2B, 12% @ >=8B, 18% @ >=12B. (We can adjust thresholds.)
- Overage: standard overage rate = list_per_token * 1.05 (5% premium) OR true-up credit applied at the end of the month if overall quarterly commit target is met.
- Burst protection: automatic burst allowance up to 150% of committed month with surcharge or offset credit (negotiable).
- Invoicing: monthly invoices; we can provide a monthly true-up that applies credits/adjustments the following invoice.

Questions for you so I can firm numbers:
1) Can you share an expected week-by-week token curve (just ballpark is fine) for the launch month?
2) Is Launch Labs open to a small initial commit (Sept) with a firm escalation step in Oct and Nov (we typically do step-up commits for launches)?

I'll loop in Finance (Marissa) and Pricing (Rishi) once we have the confirmed curve so they can approve final tiers.

Attachment: Launch_Labs_Monthly_Commit_v1.pdf (pricing table, sample ramp)

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwoodinference.com
From: Elena Park <elena@launchlabs.com>

Cc: Launch Labs Procurement <procurement@launchlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch volume phasing & commit Qs

Camila — appreciate the fast turnaround and the draft. A few clarifications from procurement and product ops:

- Week-by-week curve: we can share a private spreadsheet. Expected shape: soft ramp in week 0–1, spike in weeks 2–4 (peaks ~15B token equivalent for those weeks), then step down to 6–8B/mo. We prefer to model by weekly expected median/95th percentiles.
- Overage handling: procurement strongly prefers a true-up/credit mechanism rather than high overage rates. Can you confirm what lookback window you use for true-up (monthly vs quarterly)?
- Carry-forward/unused credits: Launch Labs will demand the ability to carry unused committed units forward at least one month due to unpredictable launch timing.
- Token definition: need clarity on how you count client streaming tokens vs standard generation tokens (we use streaming extensively). Are streaming tokens charged differently?

If you can address these, procurement is likely to move quickly. Will share the detailed weekly curve by end of day.

Thanks,
Elena
From: camila_reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@launchlabs.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch volume phasing & commit Qs

Elena — thanks for the clarifications and for committing to share the weekly curve. Looping in Rishi (Pricing) and Marissa (Revenue Ops) to get alignment on true-up and carry-forward.

Summary of proposed updates in the attached revision (Launch_Labs_Commit_Revisions_v2.xlsx):
- True-up window: monthly true-up by default; option to consolidate into a single quarterly true-up if helpful for quarterly finance reconciliation.
- Carry-forward: allow 1-month carry-forward of unused committed units (carry-forward applies only once).
- Streaming token treatment: streaming tokens counted as equivalent units but we apply a 0.9x multiplier for calculation of committed usage (i.e., streaming tokens are slightly discounted in unit accounting to reflect smaller per-request compute).
- Burst protection: automatic burst up to 150% of committed month with a surcharge of 10% on overage units above that threshold, OR we can instead provide a one-time promotional overage credit equal to 100% of first-month overage (we typically reserve that for new customers/launches).
- Promotional concession: we can offer a one-time overage credit for Oct up to 1.5B tokens if Launch Labs signs a 6-month commit and a mutual action plan that confirms launch dates.

Action items:
- Elena to share weekly expected token curve (you mentioned end of day).
- Rishi/Marissa to review revised schedule and confirm discounts and the promotional credit.

Thanks — Rishi/Marissa, any objections to the 1-month carry-forward and the 0.9x streaming multiplier?

Best,
Camila

Team — reviewed the revised schedule. Approve the structure with the following modifications so we can finalize with product:

- Discount schedule (final): 5% @ >=2B, 15% @ >=8B, 22% @ >=12B, 28% @ >=25B (these apply to the committed monthly bucket pricing; overages billed at list*1.05 unless true-up qualifies for rebate).
- Promotional credits: approve one-time Oct overage credit up to 1.5B tokens if legal signs SOW within 10 business days of the DocuSign link.

- Surge protection: allow bursts to 150% of commit; overage above 150% billed at list * 1.20 unless we invoke surge reserve (see SOW).
- Ask Marissa to confirm invoicing cadence and whether revenue needs a quarterly true-up option for recognition.

Marissa — please confirm finance OK on the promo credit and on invoice cadence being monthly with an optional quarterly true-up for ARR recognition.

Elena — attaching the final pricing table and SOW draft (SOW_draft.docx). Summary below so procurement can review quickly:

Final commercial summary (6-month agreement):
- Commit schedule (months 1–6):
  - Sep: 2.0B tokens (5% discount)
  - Oct: 8.0B tokens (15% discount) + promotional overage credit up to 1.5B tokens (conditional on signed SOW within 10 business days)
  - Nov: 12.0B tokens (22% discount)
  - Dec–Feb: 6.0B tokens/mo (15% discount)
- Streaming tokens: counted at 0.9x for commit accounting
- Overage / burst: automatic burst up to 150% of monthly commit; overage above 150% billed at list * 1.20. Standard overages inside burst band billed at list*1.05 unless true-up qualifies for rebate.
- Carry-forward: 1-month carry-forward for unused committed units (single use)
- Invoicing: monthly invoices; optional quarterly true-up for finance/ARR.
- SLA / Ops: Redwood will prioritize capacity routing for committed customers during launch windows and provide runbooks and a technical on-call during launch week.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm the weekly curve and approval of the Sep/Oct/Nov commit amounts.
2) I'll provision a DocuSign envelope (link below) with the SOW and pricing appendix. Sign + return within 10 business days to secure the promotional credit.
3) Post-signature: Redwood will set up a weekly launch ops cadence and provide an engagement playbook.
